invariants.label: Regime Validity
invariants.statement: A regime is valid only if it can enforce at least one constraint on at least one governed structure. A regime that cannot demonstrate active constraint enforcement has no structural authority — it is a nominal regime only.
invariants.formal: valid(R) ⟺ ∃C ∈ constraints(R), ∃S ∈ governed(R): enforces(R, C, S)
invariants.corollary: Nominal regimes — those that declare constraints but cannot enforce them — are structurally equivalent to absent regimes. Their constraint declarations carry no binding force under this invariant.
invariants.violation: Treating a regime as valid when it cannot enforce any constraint on any governed structure; treating declared constraints as binding without enforcement capacity.

invariants.label: Authority Decay
invariants.statement: Regime authority diminishes monotonically if enforcement actions produce no observable compliance response. Each enforcement cycle without compliance decreases the regime's authority measure α by a decay function d(α, n) where n is the enforcement cycle count without compliance.
invariants.corollary: Authority is not self-sustaining — it requires observable compliance feedback to remain at current levels. A regime that stops enforcing or stops receiving compliance signals is in structural decay, regardless of its formal declarations.
invariants.violation: Treating regime authority as stable across enforcement cycles that produce no compliance response; assuming declared authority is structurally equivalent to demonstrated authority.

decay_function.description: d(α, n) = α · (1 - λ)^n where λ ∈ (0,1) is the decay rate and n is the count of enforcement cycles without observed compliance.

parameters.λ: Decay rate — regime-specific, declared in regime configuration
parameters.n: Enforcement cycles elapsed without compliance response

decay_function.floor: α approaches but does not reach 0 asymptotically. Regime dissolution (α = 0) requires a separate structural event — collapse — not mere decay.

cross_references: INV-OR-002 (Book 4 Revelation Threshold — authority decay parallels opacity increase)

invariants.label: Regime Closure
invariants.statement: A regime cannot govern itself without introducing a meta-regime or producing a structural paradox. Self-governance violates the structural separation between governing and governed nodes required by the regime constraint model.
invariants.formal: ¬∃R: R ∈ governed(R)  [without meta-regime M: governs(M, R)]
invariants.corollary: Any system that appears to be self-governing is either (a) governed by an implicit meta-regime that must be made explicit, or (b) in structural paradox, which constitutes a regime failure condition.
invariants.violation: Placing a regime in its own governed set without declaring an explicit meta-regime; treating self-referential governance as structurally valid.

meta_regime_handling.description: When self-governance is required by design, declare a meta-regime M that governs R. M may have a distinct authority structure, decay rate, and constraint set from R. The meta-regime chain terminates at an ungoverned root — a regime that is declared as the terminal authority with no meta-regime above it.

cross_references: INV-004 (Book 1 Ontological Primacy — structural self-reference is prohibited)

invariants.label: Constraint Legitimacy
invariants.statement: Governed structures may challenge regime constraints only through declared structural channels, not by unilateral violation. A constraint challenge that bypasses declared channels is structurally classified as a violation event, not a legitimate challenge.
invariants.formal: challenge_legitimate(S, C, R) ⟺ challenge_path(S, C, R) ⊆ declared_channels(R)
invariants.corollary: Declared channels are a structural property of the regime, enumerated in its configuration. A governed structure's challenge to a constraint has no structural standing unless it proceeds through at least one declared channel.
invariants.violation: Classifying a unilateral constraint bypass as a legitimate challenge; treating the absence of declared channels as permission to challenge by any means; allowing channel-less regimes to claim legitimacy immunity.
channel_types: formal_objection: A structured declaration of non-compliance sent through the regime's declared objection interface
appeal: A challenge routed through a declared review authority above the enforcing regime node
renegotiation: A constraint modification request through the regime's declared amendment process
exit: Withdrawal from the governed set through a declared exit procedure
cross_references: INV-TEL-003 (Book 5 Compositionality — challenge paths must be explicitly encoded)
